title: Rejecting round debits or halts
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, choose the forward and find-mode settings, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. Let $c$ be a halted configuration of $B$ on $x$ with empty output, let $w$ be a Boolean word, and let $f$ be a configuration of $F$ on $x$. There is a time $t\le 2|w|+4$ such that the host run from the non-startup call on $c$ with release clear, stop flag false, counter word $w$, and fuel configuration $f$ has the following outcome: if the fixed-width decrement of $w$ succeeds, the resulting configuration is the released non-startup call on the configuration obtained from $c$ by setting its state to $a$, with the decremented word as counter and no stop flag; if the decrement fails, the resulting configuration is halted and its output is empty in find mode and the one-bit word false otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean finite machines B and F
replaced:
Let $c$ be a halted body configuration with empty output, $w$ a counter word, and $f$ a
fuel configuration. Then there is a time $t \le 2|w| + 4$ such that, from the stopped
call on $c$ with stop flag $\mathrm{false}$: if the fixed-width decrement of $w$
succeeds, the loop host at time $t$ is at the released next-anchor call with the
decremented counter word; otherwise the host at time $t$ has halted with output empty in
find mode and the single bit $\mathrm{false}$ in decision mode.
